items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: I was in Milwaukee with Woody Herman... 'oh you’re playing with Woody Herman.' And I said, 'yes.' And she said, 'does he play ‘Woodchopper’s Ball’?' And I said, 'oh yes, every night.'

ctx.x: Yeah. I’ve been thinking recently, we’re a similar age, and I think about the term “making it” in the music business. Because when we were younger and we wanted to “make it” in the music business, and what that might have meant. Do you remember what that meant for you when you were like a teenager?

Well it meant being accepted by people who were older than you. When I was 16 I was in the New Zealand Radio Orchestra, which meant I was a government employee at 16. So I would get done with school, take a bus in and be in the studio with all these guys who were far older than I was. But at that stage I had essentially made it, because I was treated not as a kid, but I was treated as an equal. And that’s really important. And the other thing that, when people say “making it,” when I look back to the Maynard…
Did you have — I don’t know how to ask this — did you have a concept, like they think you might have?
